newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel and Palestinians sign accord on debts.
newsitem.headline: Israel and Palestinians sign accord on debts.

text.p: Israel and the Palestinian Authority have signed an agreement to settle mutual debts, Israel's Treasury said on Saturday.
The Treasury said in a statement both sides on Friday signed the deal hammered out on Wednesday by Israeli Finance Minister Dan Meridor and Nabil Shaath, Palestinian minister of economic cooperation.

"Israel will transfer to the Palestinian Authority a sum of 105 million shekels ($30 million)," the statement said, specifying that 65 million shekels covered value added tax from May to December 1994.

The statement said the Palestinian Authority had committed itself to settle debts to Bezek Israel Telcom and Israeli hospitals within two weeks and that a deal to clear debts owed the Mekorot water company would be reached within three months.
The Treasury said this week the Authority owed a total of 75 million shekels to the Israeli institutions.
The Treasury statement said joint economic committees would move on to discuss abiding by trade rules agreed to in an interim economic accord, on transfers of tax receipts and on stolen vehicles.
